title: Ich hätte gern ein Brötchen
summary: Ordering politely at the Bäckerei and café — ich hätte gern, ich nehme, für mich, bitte

blocks.title: Zwei Wege zu bestellen
blocks.body: There are two everyday ways to order in German. **Ich hätte gern…** (I would like…) is soft and polite — the safe default anywhere. **Ich nehme…** (I'll take…) is direct and quick, fine once you've decided. Both end with **bitte** to keep it warm. Add **für mich** (for me) when you're ordering as part of a group.

rows: Ich hätte gern… — I would like…
für mich, bitte — for me, please
pointing out your item in a group

blocks.title: Tap to hear the ordering phrases

pairs.note: Same order, different register — *hätte gern* is a touch softer, *nehme* a touch faster. Neither is rude.

blocks.prompt: You've just decided what you want — which phrase fits best?
blocks.explain: *Ich nehme…* — direct and decisive, perfect once you've made up your mind.

blocks.prompt: Type the polite way to order a coffee: 'I would like a coffee.'
blocks.explain: *Ich hätte gern einen Kaffee.* — *der Kaffee* becomes *einen Kaffee* in the accusative.

blocks.scene: Lena play-acts as the Bäckereiverkäuferin so you can practice your order before the real thing.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.target: Guten Tag! Was hätten Sie gern?
lines.en: Good day! What would you like?
lines.spotlight: Lena switches to *Sie* — the shop-counter register, even in practice.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Ich hätte gern zwei Brötchen und einen Kaffee, bitte.
lines.en: I'd like two rolls and a coffee, please.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.en: To eat in or to go?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.target: Das macht dann sechs Euro fünfzig.
lines.en: That'll be six euros fifty, then.
